-m3-1-h06","printedPage":75,"pdfPage":93,"facts":[{"text":"The hypothalamus , a small area just ventral to the thalamus (Figures 3.10 and 3.12), has widespread connections with the rest of the Consequently, the dorsal–ventral axis of the human brain is at a right angle to the dorsal–ventral axis of the spinal cord.","The spinal cord communicates with all the sense organs and muscles except those of the head.","The cell bodies of the sensory neurons are in clusters of neurons outside the spinal cord, called the dorsal root ganglia. Because the flow of sinus fluids is a parasympathetic response, drugs that block the parasympathetic system inhibit sinus flow.","Certain decongestant pills containing pseudoephedrine have been withdrawn or restricted because of their potential for abuse.","Some neuroscientists prefer terms with Greek roots: rhombencephalon (hindbrain), mesencephalon (midbrain), and prosencephalon (forebrain).","The hindbrain, the posterior part of the brain, consists of the medulla, the pons, and the cerebellum.","The medulla and pons, the midbrain, and certain central structures of the forebrain constitute the brainstem (Figure 3.8).","In elephants, the trigeminal nerve that receives sensations from the face is huge because it innervates the trunk, a highly sensitive structure for elephants. Cerebral Cortex","kind":"detailed_source_grounded_notes","printedStart":81,"printedEnd":90,"pdfStart":99,"pdfEnd":108,"content":[{"type":"paragraph","text":"The cerebral cortex has layers, columns, and interconnected regions. Its occipital, parietal, temporal, and frontal lobes contribute to different functions, but complex behavior depends on communication across areas."},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The module discusses the prefrontal cortex and the limitations of assigning a complete mental ability to just one location. Use the connections among areas to think about the binding problem and coordinated processing."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m3-2-study-1","text":"Cortex: layers, columns, and connections"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The cerebral cortex is the folded outer part of the cerebral hemispheres. Its neurons are organized in layers and interconnected local circuits, and groups of cells can share response properties in columns. The amount and arrangement of cortical tissue vary among species and individuals. The cortex is highly differentiated, but no area acts independently: communication among regions is central to almost every complex function. White-matter connections are as important as familiar gray-matter regions."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m3-2-study-2","text":"The four lobes"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The occipital lobe is particularly involved in vision; the parietal lobe contributes to body-related sensation and spatial processing; the temporal lobe participates in hearing, object recognition, and aspects of memory; and frontal regions contribute to movement, planning, and control. These are broad associations, not rigid boundaries. A perceptual or cognitive task typically recruits multiple areas, and damage effects depend on the location and extent of injury as well as connections disrupted."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m3-2-study-3","text":"Prefrontal cortex and behavior"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Prefrontal regions help maintain goals, regulate actions, inhibit unsuitable responses, and organize behavior over time. Historical prefrontal lobotomies illustrate the severe human cost of intervening in brain systems before understanding their roles and risks. Modern research asks not just whether frontal cortex is active during a task but which processes and connections are necessary. Inhibition is a genuine achievement: deciding not to act can require neural control as much as deciding to move."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m3-2-study-4","text":"Avoid the localization trap"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"It is useful to associate functions with brain areas, but it is inaccurate to claim that one small cortical patch uniquely contains a skill such as 'thinking' or 'personality.' Sensory information is processed through distributed hierarchies and recurrent communication. When interpreting a scan or lesion, distinguish involvement from exclusivity. Cortical specialization and cooperation are simultaneously true."},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-2-h01","text":"Organization of the Cerebral Cortex"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The microscopic structure of neurons varies from one cortical area to another, as does their density per volume .","sourcePrintedPage":82,"sourcePdfPage":100,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In humans and most other mammals, the cerebral cortex contains up to six distinct laminae , layers of cell bodies parallel to the surface of the cortex (Figure 3.20).","sourcePrintedPage":82,"sourcePdfPage":100,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The laminae vary in prominence from one part of the cortex to another, and a given lamina may be absent from certain areas.","sourcePrintedPage":82,"sourcePdfPage":100,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Lamina IV, which receives sensory information, is prominent in the sensory areas of the cortex but absent from the motor cortex.","sourcePrintedPage":82,"sourcePdfPage":100,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Lamina V, which sends long axons to the spinal cord, is thickest in the motor cortex.","sourcePrintedPage":82,"sourcePdfPage":100,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Layer I, with many axons and dendrites but few cells, is a site for many connections, including those that are essential for learning.","sourcePrintedPage":82,"sourcePdfPage":100,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The cells of the cortex are also organized into columns of cells perpendicular to the laminae.","sourcePrintedPage":82,"sourcePdfPage":100,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-2-h02","text":"The Occipital Lobe"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"We group the areas of cortex into four lobes named for the skull bones that lie over them: occipital, parietal, temporal, and frontal.","sourcePrintedPage":83,"sourcePdfPage":101,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The posterior pole of the occipital lobe is called the primary visual cortex , or striate cortex , because of its striped appearance in cross section.","sourcePrintedPage":83,"sourcePdfPage":101,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Damage in the striate cortex causes cortical blindness in the related part of the visual field.","sourcePrintedPage":83,"sourcePdfPage":101,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"damage to the striate cortex of the right hemisphere causes blindness in the left visual field (the left side of the world from the viewer’s perspective).","sourcePrintedPage":83,"sourcePdfPage":101,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People who experience eye damage become blind, but if they have an intact occipital cortex and previous visual experience, they can still have visual imagery and visual dreams .","sourcePrintedPage":83,"sourcePdfPage":101,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-2-h03","text":"The Parietal Lobe"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The parietal lobe lies between the occipital lobe and the central sulcus , a deep groove in the surface of the cortex (Figure 3.23).","sourcePrintedPage":83,"sourcePdfPage":101,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The area just posterior to the central sulcus, the postcentral gyrus , or primary somatosensory cortex , receives sensations from touch receptors, muscle-stretch receptors, and joint receptors.","sourcePrintedPage":83,"sourcePdfPage":101,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Brain surgeons sometimes use only local anesthesia, anesthetizing the scalp but leaving the brain awake.","sourcePrintedPage":83,"sourcePdfPage":101,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Two of the bands receive mostly light-touch information, one receives deep-pressure information, and one receives a combination of both .","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Information about touch and body location is important not only for its own sake but also for interpreting visual and auditory information.","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The parietal lobe monitors the information about eye, head, and body positions and passes it on to brain areas that control movement.","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The parietal lobe is essential not only for spatial information but also numerical information .","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-2-h04","text":"The Temporal Lobe"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The temporal lobe , the lateral portion of each hemisphere, near the temples (Figure 3.22), is the primary cortical target","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The human temporal lobe— mainly the left temporal lobe for most people—is essential for speech.","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The temporal lobe also contributes to complex aspects of vision, including perception of movement and recognition of faces and other objects.","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When patients with schizophrenia report hallucinations, brain scans detect activity in the temporal lobes .","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Frequent auditory hallucinations are related to thinner than average auditory cortex in the left temporal lobe .","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Temporal lobe damage can lead to a set of behaviors known as the Klüver-Bucy syndrome .","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The investigators who first described it reported that monkeys failed to display normal fears and anxieties after temporal lobe damage.","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Klüver-Bucy syndrome also occurs occasionally in humans after temporal lobe damage, where the most common symptoms are inappropriate sexual behaviors, overeating, and excessive lip-smacking or other mouth movements .","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-2-h05","text":"The Frontal Lobe"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The frontal lobe , containing the primary motor cortex and the prefrontal cortex, extends from the central sulcus to the anterior limit of the brain (Figure 3.22).","sourcePrintedPage":85,"sourcePdfPage":103,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Its posterior portion, the precentral gyrus , is specialized for the control of fine movements, such as moving a finger.","sourcePrintedPage":85,"sourcePdfPage":103,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Each area along that gyrus controls one part of the body, mostly on the contralateral (opposite) side.","sourcePrintedPage":85,"sourcePdfPage":103,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The most anterior portion of the frontal lobe is the prefrontal cortex .","sourcePrintedPage":85,"sourcePdfPage":103,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For example, it occupies almost twice as high a percentage of the human brain as it does of a monkey brain .","sourcePrintedPage":85,"sourcePdfPage":103,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Several areas in the prefrontal cortex and the temporoparietal junction have come to be known as the default network .","sourcePrintedPage":85,"sourcePdfPage":103,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"We often assume that daydreaming is unimportant, but it prepares us for decisions we might have to face later.","sourcePrintedPage":85,"sourcePdfPage":103,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The default network is also active when your brain replays recent experiences, an important process for storing memories .","sourcePrintedPage":85,"sourcePdfPage":103,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-2-h06","text":"The Rise and Fall of Prefrontal Lobotomies"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Lobotomy began after a report in 1935 that damaging the prefrontal cortex of laboratory primates made them tamer without noticeably impairing their sensations or coordination.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A few physicians reasoned loosely—uh, very loosely—that the same operation might help people with severe psychiatric disorders.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In their defense, this was a time when psychiatrists had no effective treatment for severe disorders.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"His techniques were crude, even by the standards of the time, using such instruments as an electric drill and a metal pick.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Freeman began lobotomizing people with less serious problems, including some people whom we would consider mentally healthy by today’s standards.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When drug therapies became available in the mid-1950s, lobotomies quickly dropped out of favor.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Among the common consequences of prefrontal lobotomy were apathy, lack of initiative, memory disorders, distractibility, and a loss of emotional expressions .","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People with prefrontal damage often acted impulsively because they were unable to calculate adequately the probable outcomes of their behaviors.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-2-h07","text":"Functions of the Prefrontal Cortex"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"An analysis of thousands of studies concluded that the prefrontal cortex has three major regions .","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The posterior portion is associated mostly with movement.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The middle zone pertains to cognitive control, emotional reactions, and certain aspects of memory.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"After damage in this area, people can learn that stimulus A is better than B, and that B is better than C, but they might not infer that A is better than C.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"They form memories, but they often don’t apply them to new situations .","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The anterior zone of the prefrontal cortex is important for making decisions, evaluating which of several courses of action is likely to achieve the best outcome.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Cells in the prefrontal cortex respond to these complex factors .","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People with prefrontal cortical damage often make decisions that seem impulsive, because they have difficulty weighing all the likely pros and cons.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-2-h08","text":"Beyond Gray Matter: The Connections"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Historically, most researchers have concentrated more on the cell bodies (gray matter) than on the connections among them (white matter).","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, behavior and experience depend on the communication among cells, and that depends on the connections.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The Human Connectome Project is an effort to map all the long-distance connections, analogous to the way the human genome project mapped all the genes on the chromosomes.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers have already demonstrated many correlations between brain connections and behavioral tendencies, and they expect to find abnormal connections responsible for many psychological disorders .","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-2-h09","text":"How Do the Parts Work Together?"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Vision, touch, and hearing activate cortical areas that have only weak connections with one another.","sourcePrintedPage":87,"sourcePdfPage":105,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Even in vision, the area that responds to shape is separate from the area responsible for seeing the object’s color, the area detecting its movement, and the area detecting its location in space.","sourcePrintedPage":87,"sourcePdfPage":105,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Karl Lashley noticed this problem long ago, but neuroscientists did not pay much attention to it until the 1990s. 1","sourcePrintedPage":87,"sourcePdfPage":105,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The question of how various brain areas produce a perception of a single object is known as the binding problem , or large-scale integration problem.","sourcePrintedPage":87,"sourcePdfPage":105,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In an earlier era, researchers assumed that various kinds of sensory information converge in areas that associate one sensation with another.","sourcePrintedPage":87,"sourcePdfPage":105,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, all information does not feed into a central “little person in the head.” Relatively few cells combine one sense with another .","sourcePrintedPage":87,"sourcePdfPage":105,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"As part of this illusion, the visual stimulus alters the response of the auditory cortex, so that the sound really does seem to come from the same location as the dummy’s mouth .","sourcePrintedPage":87,"sourcePdfPage":105,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In contrast, if you watch a poorly dubbed foreignlanguage film, the lips do not move at the same time as the speech, and you perceive that the words did not come from those lips.","sourcePrintedPage":87,"sourcePdfPage":105,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Applying these principles, researchers arranged a camera to video someone’s back, and they simultaneously sent the pictures to a three-dimensional display mounted to the person’s head, as in Figure 3.25.","sourcePrintedPage":87,"sourcePdfPage":105,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"So, the evidence indicates that we bind two experiences that occur at the same time.","sourcePrintedPage":88,"sourcePdfPage":106,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-2-h10","text":"In Closing: Functions of the Cerebral Cortex"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The cerebral cortex is the largest portion of the human brain, but it is not the entire brain.","sourcePrintedPage":88,"sourcePdfPage":106,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Its primary function seems to be one of elaborating sensory information and organizing sequences of behaviors.","sourcePrintedPage":88,"sourcePdfPage":106,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Even fish, which have no cerebral cortex, can see and hear, but the cerebral cortex enables us to add great complexity.","sourcePrintedPage":88,"sourcePdfPage":106,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"They’re also presented in alphabetical order with definitions in the book’s Subject Index/Glossary, at the end of this book.","sourcePrintedPage":89,"sourcePdfPage":107,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When monkeys with Klüver-Bucy syndrome pick up lighted matches and snakes, we do not know whether they are displaying an emotional deficit or an inability to identify the object.","sourcePrintedPage":89,"sourcePdfPage":107,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"bullet","text":"For example, if one cell in a column responds to touch on the palm of the left hand, then the other cells in that column do, too.","headingId":"bp14-m3-2-h01","sourcePrintedPage":83,"sourcePdfPage":101},{"type":"bullet","text":"If one cell responds to a horizontal pattern of light at a particular location, then other cells in the column respond to the same pattern in nearby locations.","headingId":"bp14-m3-2-h01","sourcePrintedPage":83,"sourcePdfPage":101},{"type":"bullet","text":"The occipital lobe, at the posterior (caudal) end of the cortex, is the main target for visual information.","headingId":"bp14-m3-2-h02","sourcePrintedPage":83,"sourcePdfPage":101},{"type":"bullet","text":"A person with complete cortical blindness has normal eyes and pupillary reflexes, but no conscious visual perception and no visual imagery (not even in dreams).","headingId":"bp14-m3-2-h02","sourcePrintedPage":83,"sourcePdfPage":101},{"type":"bullet","text":"In short, the eyes provide the stimulus, and the visual cortex provides the experience.","headingId":"bp14-m3-2-h02","sourcePrintedPage":83,"sourcePdfPage":101},{"type":"bullet","text":"If during this process they lightly stimulate the postcentral gyrus, people report tingling sensations on the opposite side of the body.","headingId":"bp14-m3-2-h03","sourcePrintedPage":83,"sourcePdfPage":101},{"type":"bullet","text":"Separate areas along each band receive simultaneous information from different parts of the body, as illustrated in Figure 3.23a.","headingId":"bp14-m3-2-h03","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102},{"type":"bullet","text":"For example, if a person sees something in the upper-left portion of the visual field, their brain needs to know in which direction their eyes are turned, the position of their head, and the tilt of their body before it can determine the location of what they see.","headingId":"bp14-m3-2-h03","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102},{"type":"bullet","text":"The temporal lobes are also important for emotional and motivational behaviors.","headingId":"bp14-m3-2-h04","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102},{"type":"bullet","text":"The area where the parietal lobe and the temporal lobe meet, close also to the occipital .","printedPage":87,"pdfPage":105,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":79},{"text":"As part of this illusion, the visual stimulus alters the response of .","printedPage":87,"pdfPage":105,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":80},{"text":"In contrast, if you watch a poorly dubbed foreignlanguage film, the Lamina IV, which receives sensory information, is prominent in the sensory areas of the cortex but absent from the motor cortex.","Lamina V, which sends long axons to the spinal cord, is thickest in the motor cortex.","Layer I, with many axons and dendrites but few cells, is a site for many connections, including those that are essential for learning. The cells of the cortex are also organized into columns of cells perpendicular to the laminae.","We group the areas of cortex into four lobes named for the skull bones that lie over them: occipital, parietal, temporal, and frontal.","The posterior pole of the occipital lobe is called the primary visual cortex, or striate cortex, because of its striped appearance in cross section.","Damage in the striate cortex causes cortical blindness in the related part of the visual field. damage to the striate cortex of the right hemisphere causes blindness in the left visual field (the left side of the world from the viewer’s perspective).","People who experience eye damage become blind, but if they have an intact occipital cortex and previous visual experience, they can still have visual imagery and visual dreams.","The parietal lobe lies between the occipital lobe and the central sulcus, a deep groove in the surface of the cortex (Figure 3.23).","The area just posterior to the central sulcus, the postcentral gyrus, or primary somatosensory cortex, receives sensations from touch receptors, muscle-stretch receptors, and joint receptors.","Brain surgeons sometimes use only local anesthesia, anesthetizing the scalp but leaving the brain awake. Two of the bands receive mostly light-touch information, one receives deep-pressure information, and one receives a combination of both.","Information about touch and body location is important not only for its own sake but also for interpreting visual and auditory information.","The parietal lobe monitors the information about eye, head, and body positions and passes it on to brain areas that control movement. The parietal lobe is essential not only for spatial information but also numerical information.","The temporal lobe, the lateral portion of each hemisphere, near the temples (Figure 3.22), is the primary cortical target","The human temporal lobe— mainly the left temporal lobe for most people—is essential for speech.","The temporal lobe also contributes to complex aspects of vision, including perception of movement and recognition of faces and other objects. When patients with schizophrenia report hallucinations, brain scans detect activity in the temporal lobes.","Frequent auditory hallucinations are related to thinner than average auditory cortex in the left temporal lobe.","Temporal lobe damage can lead to a set of behaviors known as the Klüver-Bucy syndrome.","The investigators who first described it reported that monkeys failed to display normal fears and anxieties after temporal lobe damage. Klüver-Bucy syndrome also occurs occasionally in humans after temporal lobe damage, where the most common symptoms are inappropriate sexual behaviors, overeating, and excessive lip-smacking or other mouth movements.","The frontal lobe, containing the primary motor cortex and the prefrontal cortex, extends from the central sulcus to the anterior limit of the brain (Figure 3.22).","Its posterior portion, the precentral gyrus, is specialized for the control of fine movements, such as moving a finger.","Each area along that gyrus controls one part of the body, mostly on the contralateral (opposite) side. The most anterior portion of the frontal lobe is the prefrontal cortex.","For example, it occupies almost twice as high a percentage of the human brain as it does of a monkey brain.","Several areas in the prefrontal cortex and the temporoparietal junction have come to be known as the default network.","We often assume that daydreaming is unimportant, but it prepares us for decisions we might have to face later. The default network is also active when your brain replays recent experiences, an important process for storing memories.","Lobotomy began after a report in 1935 that damaging the prefrontal cortex of laboratory primates made them tamer without noticeably impairing their sensations or coordination.","A few physicians reasoned loosely—uh, very loosely—that the same operation might help people with severe psychiatric disorders.","In their defense, this was a time when psychiatrists had no effective treatment for severe disorders. His techniques were crude, even by the standards of the time, using such instruments as an electric drill and a metal pick.","Freeman began lobotomizing people with less serious problems, including some people whom we would consider mentally healthy by today’s standards.","When drug therapies became available in the mid-1950s, lobotomies quickly dropped out of favor.","Among the common consequences of prefrontal lobotomy were apathy, lack of initiative, memory disorders, distractibility, and a loss of emotional expressions. People with prefrontal damage often acted impulsively because they were unable to calculate adequately the probable outcomes of their behaviors.","An analysis of thousands of studies concluded that the prefrontal cortex has three major regions.","The posterior portion is associated mostly with movement.","The middle zone pertains to cognitive control, emotional reactions, and certain aspects of memory. After damage in this area, people can learn that stimulus A is better than B, and that B is better than C, but they might not infer that A is better than C.","They form memories, but they often don’t apply them to new situations.","The anterior zone of the prefrontal cortex is important for making decisions, evaluating which of several courses of action is likely to achieve the best outcome.","Cells in the prefrontal cortex respond to these complex factors. People with prefrontal cortical damage often make decisions that seem impulsive, because they have difficulty weighing all the likely pros and cons.","Historically, most researchers have concentrated more on the cell bodies (gray matter) than on the connections among them (white matter).","However, behavior and experience depend on the communication among cells, and that depends on the connections. The Human Connectome Project is an effort to map all the long-distance connections, analogous to the way the human genome project mapped all the genes on the chromosomes.","Researchers have already demonstrated many correlations between brain connections and behavioral tendencies, and they expect to find abnormal connections responsible for many psychological disorders.","Vision, touch, and hearing activate cortical areas that have only weak connections with one another.","Even in vision, the area that responds to shape is separate from the area responsible for seeing the object’s color, the area detecting its movement, and the area detecting its location in space.","Karl Lashley noticed this problem long ago, but neuroscientists did not pay much attention to it until the 1990s. 1","The question of how various brain areas produce a perception of a single object is known as the binding problem, or large-scale integration problem. In an earlier era, researchers assumed that various kinds of sensory information converge in areas that associate one sensation with another.","However, all information does not feed into a central “little person in the head.” Relatively few cells combine one sense with another.","As part of this illusion, the visual stimulus alters the response of the auditory cortex, so that the sound really does seem to come from the same location as the dummy’s mouth.","In contrast, if you watch a poorly dubbed foreignlanguage film, the lips do not move at the same time as the speech, and you perceive that the words did not come from those lips. Applying these principles, researchers arranged a camera to video someone’s back, and they simultaneously sent the pictures to a three-dimensional display mounted to the person’s head, as in Figure 3.25.","So, the evidence indicates that we bind two experiences that occur at the same time.","The cerebral cortex is the largest portion of the human brain, but it is not the entire brain.","Its primary function seems to be one of elaborating sensory information and organizing sequences of behaviors.","Even fish, which have no cerebral cortex, can see and hear, but the cerebral cortex enables us to add great complexity.
